notes: SynQ combines QTT and tagless-final embedding to control model construction and support different interpretations. The embedding abstracts over the representation and supplies the construction operations. This page explains abstract construction first and then chooses interpretations. Thesis §4.2.1, §4.2.4 and §4.5.

Abstract the component representation. The diagram and schematic expression compose foo then bar. foo and bar are assumed supplied in the surrounding context; this fragment is not a complete standalone definition that has newly been checked.

Multiplicity 0 prevents inspecting the abstract representation type. Together with the supplied component operations, this controls the vocabulary available for constructing models. Zero alone does not establish semantic alignment or guarantee the meaning of an arbitrary backend. Thesis §4.2.1 and §4.2.4.

Assume an operation that composes components sharing state. The interpretation supplies this operation consistently with the abstract representation. Instantiation means supplying a representation and its operations, not replacing a type name as text.
The resulting component has state s, input a and output c. Follow the type indices and the highlighted result fragment.

The model expression composes foo then bar using the supplied operation. The written expression bar =<< foo has function argument order opposite the data-flow order. The explanations accumulate; the active guide moves to this expression.

Now choose an interpretation of this same model. The code compacts into the route overview; the concrete sample diagram and explanation rows leave. Let the internal Morph settle; no route is revealed automatically. The interpretation supplies the meaning of these operations, including bindings and applications. Their behaviour can therefore differ from Idris2’s own evaluation strategy. This is not a general theorem of semantic equivalence for arbitrary backends.

Choose executable functions to evaluate the model. Instantiate seq and the supplied composition operation consistently. The denotation is an Idris2 function. These are the interpretation and reasoning routes in the overview from P9; constructing models belongs to modelling, while interpretations and transformations are design steps.

Choose an intermediate representation, or IR, to build a structured model. Other EDSLs/IRs is a real intermediate level of the framework. The circular route also represents a model-to-model interpretation or transformation. This route overview does not itself prove that all interpretations are correct.

Attach properties in types. The Idris2 enclosure and label show the host-language context, while the delayed property links relate representations and reasoning. Construction restrictions and semantic alignment depend on the embedding and supplied interpretations, not only on a visible 0 annotation.

Use the IR route to generate the Verilog HDL example. Its framework route and target appear on this click. The complete original example is visible before the LLVM reveal. This is a reused source example, not new experimental output.

Use the IR route to generate the LLVM IR example on the next click. Its panel appears in front of the lower part of the Verilog example, following the overlapping arrangement in AEiC P20. The Verilog header and upper code remain visible behind it; reverse one click to read the full Verilog example. Both are reused source examples, not new experimental output.
